Repo line-ending policy (owner call, still open, but the urgent half is CLOSED as of 2026-07-27). The rationale previously recorded here -- 'building on the WSL /mnt/c mount emits CRLF and produces a 3,177-line content-free diff' -- was a wrong diagnosis. The mount was a bystander. The real cause was preprocess-sections.sh trapping a CRLF record's trailing CR *inside* the bold markers it generates (`**Header<CR>**`) and writing that back into the source; a lone CR makes git classify the file as non-text, which silently disables core.autocrlf=input for it, so its CRLF endings then diff against CI's LF blobs on every line. Script fixed at source and the 11 committed occurrences repaired (8a0fd27f), so the phantom-diff symptom is gone and a local build is no longer expected to churn. What remains genuinely open, and is a much weaker case: 50 of 95 section sources still carry CRLF in the working tree, harmless under autocrlf=input but re-armed the moment any future generator does substring surgery on a record. A narrow `.gitattributes` (`*.md text eol=lf`) would remove the hazard class entirely at the cost of a one-time normalization of those 50 files. dp's call; no longer urgent.

notes: 2026-08-24 run: ONE in-place amendment to 15-dark-matter, and its main content is a REFUSAL to propagate. The window's finding (2026-08-23) concluded that the framework's two NGC 1052-DF2 repairs "invalidate the EFE = 0 premise" and inscribed in PREDICTIONS.md that "admitting ANY non-local C-contribution invalidates the C local => EFE=0 derivation globally." Refuted here by direct computation before anything reached the whitepaper: the derivation turns on C being independent of Phi (the whitepaper's own wording, "linear in Phi -- C depends on rho, not grad-Phi"), not on C being local. Solving div[C grad Phi] = 4 pi G rho on a 161^2 grid, a FULLY NON-LOCAL Phi-independent C gives EFE = 5.6e-13 (superposition exact) while a grad-Phi keyed C gives 4.6e-2 -- eleven orders apart. So C_eff = max(C(rho_local), C_formation) preserves EFE = 0 exactly, and EFE = 0 returns from "triply compromised" to DOUBLY compromised (mutually-exclusive-with-viability 08-15, screened-from-test 08-23). What the source found and mis-located is LARGER than what it claimed: both repairs abandon C = C(rho), the sector's constitutive posit. The landing site was an internal contradiction nobody had marked -- 15-dark-matter's law returns C ~ 0.04 at DF2's measured density while its own Session #97 paragraph 108 lines later asserts a "high-C core". Amended there, with two figure corrections (strict local predicts sigma = 35 km/s not 80, a ~4x miss not ~10x; recomputed sigma_N = 6.99 km/s reproduces van Dokkum+2018's published ~7) and one confirmation the source did not make (the formation-coherence repair reproduces DF2 at 8.4-9.9 km/s vs 8.5 observed, C_req = 0.68 inside its stated 0.5-0.7 band).
